description: Individual project focused on space medicine, human anatomy, and clinical infection control frameworks. Developing a conceptual bio-safety and health monitoring software architecture to mitigate physiological risks for astronauts during space missions.
summary:
For this project, we have developed a professional medical health system called 'Astro-Shield,' designed to protect the bodies and heads of astronauts during long-duration space missions. 

THE PROBLEM: In zero-gravity environments, fluid pressure increases within the human brain and eyes, while spinal discs undergo stretching, leading to pain. Furthermore, in the confined space of a cabin, astronauts—whose immune systems may be weakened—face an increased risk of infections. Our system utilizes a smart headband and sensors integrated into a spinal suit to help manage head pressure and ensure proper, aligned posture.

INFECTION AND HYGIENE CARE: To maintain a clean cabin environment, the system employs ICU-grade HEPA air filters and automated UV-C light sanitization to eliminate bacteria. 

WHY THIS IS IMPORTANT: It keeps astronauts healthy while in space, ensuring they do not face additional health complications upon their return to Earth. Additionally, by leveraging NASA’s open-access data, it contributes to advancements in future space medicine and cancer research.
details: The 'Astro Shield' system we have designed for this project is a wearable, automated health monitoring solution. It includes a headband that continuously monitors the brain and eye activity of astronauts, as well as fluid pressure. Additionally, sensors integrated into the suit detect pressure along the spine, helping to maintain proper spinal alignment. To ensure a clean, bacteria-free environment within the spacecraft cabin, we have incorporated HEPA air filters—similar to those used in hospitals—along with an automated UV-C light sanitization system. This presentation was created using Canva, and our design incorporates insights derived from open-source data provided by NASA GeneLab. Our concept is innovative because it replaces large, Earth-based medical equipment with a compact, wearable device that provides real-time support to astronauts—making it an ideal solution for long-duration missions, such as those to Mars. This system will help astronauts maintain their health and hygiene in space, while also contributing to future cancer research by facilitating the analysis of cellular data.
